logistics-dynamic-pricing.name: Dynamic Pricing Service (DPS - Supporting & Admin)
logistics-dynamic-pricing.role: Calculates dynamic delivery fees, rider surcharges, and customer subscription discounts across APAC, Europe, and Middle East platforms via gRPC & REST.
logistics-dynamic-pricing.techStack: Kotlin, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, AWS EKS, SQS, Kafka, Valkey/Redis, S3

logistics-dynamic-pricing-api.name: Dynamic Pricing API & Fallback Service
logistics-dynamic-pricing-api.role: Ultra-low-latency (<25ms) runtime pricing engine and standalone fallback service serving global checkout and cart calculations.
logistics-dynamic-pricing-api.techStack: Kotlin, Undertow, Kotlin Coroutines, Valkey / ElastiCache, FeaturesWithFriends (FwF)

logistics-deliveryareas.name: Delivery Area Service (DAS)

logistics-deliveryareas.techStack: Go / Java, PostGIS / PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis

logistics-tracking-api.name: Logistics Tracking API

incidentGuardrails.name: Non-Negative Delivery Fee Invariant
incidentGuardrails.rule: Delivery fee outputs must explicitly assert non-negative integers (`fee >= 0`). Never allow discount or incentive deductions to produce negative total delivery fees.

incidentGuardrails.name: Weather Surge Condition Enforcement
incidentGuardrails.rule: When severe weather condition flags (rain/snow) are active from LWS, assert that multiplier logic produces an active surge surcharge (`multiplier > 1.0`) and does not silently fall back to standard 1.0.

incidentGuardrails.name: Subscription Fee Waiver Continuity
incidentGuardrails.rule: Changes gating customer subscription logic must verify that fallback branches do not inadvertently charge full delivery fees to active subscription members when feature flags are toggled.

incidentGuardrails.name: S3 Precomputation Schema Sync
incidentGuardrails.rule: When modifying S3 price dataset schemas or precomputation paths in batch jobs, verify that the API runtime loader contract matches the exact S3 key schema to prevent country shard lag.

incidentGuardrails.name: Audit Logging Continuity
incidentGuardrails.rule: When modifying pricing audit log structures, ensure logging pipelines maintain non-zero event throughput and do not swallow parsing exceptions silently.

teamReviewLearnings.rule: Evaluate feature flags at the very start of service methods to enable early return and bypass redundant database or Valkey cache lookups when a feature is disabled.
When adding or modifying pricing schemes or override rules in the primary API, explicitly state and implement the expected behavior in the Fallback service (e.g. default base fee or zero discounts).

Never include high-cardinality or unbounded identifiers (e.g. customer IDs, order IDs, vendor lists, or unbounded configuration keys) as Prometheus tags or metric names to prevent Prometheus scraping OOMs.
DTO, Proto, and domain model mappers must remain pure transformation functions; do not embed business rules, validation logic, or conditional discards inside mapper classes.

Any parallelized asynchronous processing (e.g. concurrent vendor price calculations using coroutines) must include a feature flag kill-switch to revert to sequential execution under thread pool saturation.
Unit and integration tests covering feature-flagged paths must explicitly indicate the flag state in the test method name (e.g. `when<FeatureFlag>IsOff_returnsFallback()`).

Controllers must never return ad-hoc internalServerError() or raw 500 JSON responses. Throw domain exceptions and let centralized @ControllerAdvice (ApiExceptionHandler) format the response and status code.

Subscription and loyalty discounts must strictly apply only to eligible fee components (e.g. delivery fee waivers) and never cascade blindly across independent overrides like Meal-For-One (MFO) or Minimum-Order-Value (MOV).

When refactoring or pulling down service methods, ensure that external I/O operations (database queries, Redis calls, S3 fetches) remain enclosed inside an active metric Timer / span to prevent losing latency observability.
Any new environment variable or secret referenced in application.yml or bootstrap.yml must be mapped in logistics-kubernetes Helm charts before merging to avoid staging pod startup failures.

Never immediately remove or rename existing fields from public DTOs or API contracts in a single release. Annotate with @Deprecated, preserve backwards-compatible getters, and give downstream clients a deprecation window.
